def: Reverse-mode differentiation of a layered network: one backward sweep gives the gradient of the loss for every parameter.
The calculus rule that the derivative of a composition is the product of the derivatives of its parts.
The gradient of the loss with respect to a layer's output, handed backwards to that layer by the one above it.
The product of an incoming gradient with a layer's Jacobian, which backpropagation computes without ever forming the Jacobian.
A test that compares a hand-written gradient with a finite-difference estimate on a tiny network.
The intermediate tensors produced during the forward pass, which must be kept for the backward pass.
Keeping only some activations and recomputing the rest during the backward pass, to save memory at the cost of extra compute.
The gradient of the loss with respect to the logits, equal to the predicted probabilities minus the one-hot true label.
The matrix of all partial derivatives of a function's outputs with respect to its inputs.
